## Questions

**1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**

_Draft, to finish after the after run._
- **I tested the edges of the window, not the edges of "off".** Every test for "no notice" used a booking in the future. So nothing noticed that one guard was all that kept an in-progress booking cancellable on the many event types without a notice. That's the most important AC7 case.
- **Authorization was tested only on the happy path.** "No session" was tested only against a booking that had an organizer.
- **The UI tests were checked through test ids, not what users get.** No test asked whether a saved 0 shows as "off", or whether the field has an accessible name.
- **The repository queries were never run.** The service tests mocked them, so 33 mutants on the recurring rule's query had no coverage.
- **Most equivalent mutants came from my own redundant defensive code.** Examples: `?.` on fields that are always set, and a second `<= 0` check after `isWithinMinimumCancellationNotice` already checks. That suggests simplifying the code rather than adding tests.

**2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.**

_Draft._ Yes. The `||` → `&&` and `notice <= 0` → `false` survivors at `minimumCancellationNotice.ts:21` showed that my existing test "has no effect when the notice is negative" asserts a behaviour no requirement asked for. Negative notices can't be stored, so the expected value came from my implementation. Its future start time also meant it didn't even reach the branch it claims to check.

The styling survivors and the `EventAdvancedTab.tsx:831` survivor are the opposite case. Requirements give no expected value for them, so I documented them rather than writing tests that would only copy what the code currently does.

The new tests take their expected values from the ACs, the #150 discussion, WCAG, or behaviour the code already had upstream (table above).

**3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct?**

_Draft._ I used Claude Code (log in `ai-logs/sprint3/julissaehp/`, linked from the PR).
- **Configuration:** it extended the issue config to the backend's changed lines and recomputed the line ranges after merging `main`.
- **Running:** it ran the dry runs and the official before run.
- **Analysis:** it drafted the classification of all 29 survivors and the new tests.
- **What I verified:**
  - _pending_: the before and after reports have the same 313 mutants at the same locations;
  - _pending_: each "killed after" survivor shows as Killed;
  - _pending_: the scores match Stryker's summary.
- **What was corrected:**
  - **`EventAdvancedTab.tsx:831` reclassified.** The first draft called it equivalent, because the UI can't create the state where it differs. Checking the tRPC update showed that the API can save that state, so it's now a test gap left for a team decision.
  - **The `bookingActions.ts:23` estimate.** The first draft expected a new test to kill 2 uncovered mutants there. Both turned out to be equivalent once covered, so that test is kept for behaviour, not score.

# Mutation testing: Issue #139 -- Prevent attendees from cancelling within a set time before a booking

**PR(s):** [#142](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/142) (settings UI) and _backend PR for #150, add the link when the PR is opened_ (persistence and enforcement)
**Tool:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 with the Vitest runner
**Config:** [stryker.139.config.mjs](../../../stryker.139.config.mjs) and [vitest.stryker-139.config.mts](../../../vitest.stryker-139.config.mts), built on the shared [stryker.config.mjs](../../../stryker.config.mjs) by @zach-short (PR #135, carried in @zachbowden's PR #140)
**Command** (Git Bash; Stryker 10 needs Node 22, and this machine's nvm has no `exec`):
`TZ=UTC STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/139-julissaehp-<before|after>.json "$LOCALAPPDATA/Author Software/nvm/installs/v22.23.5/node.exe" node_modules/@stryker-mutator/core/bin/stryker.js run stryker.139.config.mjs`
**Reports:** [before](reports/139-julissaehp-before.json) · [after](reports/139-julissaehp-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before 65.16% → after 79.03% (covered mutants only: 87.45% → 92.45%)

### Setup notes

- **Only the executable lines #139 added or changed are mutated: 313 mutants in 18 files.**
  - This covers both PRs: #142's settings UI, and the backend PR's persistence, enforcement, booking page and bookings list.
  - Imports produce no mutants, so they are left out, as are type-only lines, the `null` default in `defaultEvents.ts` and the test builder.
  - `BookingListItem.tsx` and `BookingActionsDropdown.tsx` are in scope but produced 0 mutants. That's why the reports list 16 files.
- **The test list is explicit.**
  - The before run used the 8 test files written for #139 (175 tests).
  - The after run adds `BookingRepository.test.ts`, which holds the new repository tests, for 9 files and 191 tests. #140 also listed that file.
  - The mutated code did not change between the runs. Both reports contain the same 313 mutants at identical locations, checked by comparing file, position, mutator and replacement.
- **Stryker 10 requires Node 22 or newer**, and this machine's default is Node 20. Node 22 is called by its full path because this nvm has no `exec`.
- **`ignoreStatic` is on** (from the shared config). Values built when a module first loads are reported as Ignored in both runs: `MS_PER_MINUTE` and the error-code string in `minimumCancellationNotice.ts`, and the tRPC input schema.
- **The before run used merge commit `b3be818`, and the after run used `8222569`.** Only test files and the Vitest test list changed in between.
- **Credits:**
  - @zach-short: the shared config (#135); the `file:N-N` single-line form and leaving type-only lines out (#153).
  - @zachbowden: per-issue configs, Node 22, and this template (#140).

| Status | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Killed | 202 | 245 |
| Survived | 29 | 20 |
| No coverage | 79 | 45 |
| Ignored (static) | 3 | 3 |
| Timeout | 0 | 0 |
| Errors | 0 | 0 |

Between the runs, 10 survivors and 33 no-coverage mutants became Killed. One no-coverage mutant became Survived: the equivalent `bookingActions.ts:23` fallback, explained below. No mutant that was Killed before survived after.

## Surviving mutants

All 29 survivors from the before report are on lines #139 added or changed. The last row is the one new survivor in the after report.

A mutant is classified as equivalent in two cases. **Logic:** it gives the same result for every input. **Unreachable input:** it would differ only for an input that no part of the system can produce. In that second case the evidence for why the input is impossible is given.

| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minimumCancellationNotice.ts:21` | first guard `(!notice \|\| notice <= 0)` → `false` | Test gap (killed after) | With no notice and a booking that has already started, the mutant computes `msUntilStart < 0` and reports the booking as inside the window. The booking page and the bookings list use this helper, so every in-progress booking on every event type without a notice would lose its Cancel action. #150 AC7 says those event types keep today's behaviour, and `handleCancelBooking` accepts cancellations until the booking ends. My tests only used future start times when the notice was off. |
| `minimumCancellationNotice.ts:21` | `\|\|` → `&&`; `notice <= 0` → `false` (2 mutants) | Equivalent (unreachable input) | Both differ only for a **negative** notice. Every writer rejects negatives: the tRPC input (`int().min(0)`, see `types.test.ts` › rejects -1), the generated Prisma zod schema (`min(0)`), and duplication, which copies validated values. API v2 does not expose the field. |
| `minimumCancellationNotice.ts:21` | `notice <= 0` → `notice < 0` | Equivalent (logic) | A notice of 0 is already caught by `!notice`. |
| `minimumCancellationNotice.ts:42` | `if (!userId)` → `if (false)` | Test gap (killed after) | With no session (`userId` `null`) and a booking whose organizer is `null`, the mutant reaches `null === null` and treats an anonymous visitor as the host, who is exempt. The existing test checked "no session" only for a booking that had an organizer. Today's callers pass `undefined`, but any caller using `?? null` would open this hole. |
| `minimumCancellationNotice.ts:58` | `<` → `<=` (earliest occurrence) | Equivalent (logic) | When two start times are equal, the mutant keeps a `Date` with the same time. Callers only read the time. |
| `minimumCancellationNotice.ts:94` | `\|\|` → `&&`; `notice <= 0` → `false`; `<= 0` → `< 0` (3 mutants) | Equivalent (logic, plus unreachable input) | A missing event type implies a missing notice. A notice of 0 is caught by `!notice`. A negative notice can't be stored, and if it were, `isWithinMinimumCancellationNotice`'s own guard would still return "not within". The only difference is one extra repository query. |
| `route.ts:65` | `session?.user?.id` → `session?.user.id` | Equivalent (unreachable input) | `getServerSession` returns `null` or a session whose `user` is always set (`getServerSession.ts:101-104`). An API caller can't supply a session object. |

## Questions

**1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**

They showed that I tested the feature where I expected it to act, but not where it must stay out of the way.

- **"Off" was only tested in the future.** Every test for "no notice" used a booking in the future. So nothing noticed that one guard was all that kept an in-progress booking cancellable on the many event types without a notice. That case covers almost every existing event type, and it is exactly what #150 AC7 protects.
- **Authorization was tested only on the happy path.** "No session" was tested only against a booking with an organizer. So nothing checked that an anonymous visitor can't match a booking whose organizer is missing.
- **The UI tests were checked through test ids, not what users get.** No test asked whether a saved 0 shows as "off", or whether the field has an accessible name.
- **The repository queries were never run.** The service tests mocked them, so the 33 mutants on the recurring rule's query had no coverage at all.
- **Most of the 12 equivalent mutants came from my own redundant defensive code.** Examples: `?.` on fields that are always set, and a second `<= 0` check after `isWithinMinimumCancellationNotice` already checks. That pointed to simplifying the code rather than adding tests.
- **The remaining gap is the booking page.** Its 37 lines have no unit test because the page is hard to render in isolation. Its behaviour rests on the manual end-to-end checks, and the score reflects that.

**2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.**

Yes.
- **The negative-notice test.** The `||` → `&&` and `notice <= 0` → `false` survivors at `minimumCancellationNotice.ts:21` showed that my existing test "has no effect when the notice is negative" asserts a behaviour no requirement asked for. Negative notices can't be stored, so its expected value came from my implementation. Its start time was also in the future, so it never reached the branch it claims to check.
- **The opposite case.** For the styling survivors and `EventAdvancedTab.tsx:831` (clearing the notice when Disable Cancelling is switched off), the requirements give no expected value at all. I documented them instead of writing tests that would only copy the code's current output, which the Sprint 3 rules reject as an expected-value source.
- **The new tests** take their expected values from the ACs, the #150 discussion, WCAG, or behaviour that already existed upstream (table above).

**3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct?**

- **Running:** it ran the dry runs (313 mutants each time) and both official runs.
- **Analysis:** it drafted the classification of all 29 survivors and wrote the new tests.
- **What I verified:**
  - All 191 selected tests pass on Node 20 and Node 22 before mutation.

  - Each "killed after" survivor shows as Killed in the after report, by the test listed for it.
  - The scores match Stryker's own summary tables: 65.16% / 87.45% and 79.03% / 92.45%.
  - Each new test's expected value comes from a requirement, a documented decision or upstream behaviour, not from the code.
- **What was corrected:**
  - **`EventAdvancedTab.tsx:831` was reclassified.** The first draft called it equivalent because the UI can't create the state where it differs. Checking the tRPC update showed that the API can save that state, so it's now a test gap left for a team decision.
  - **The `bookingActions.ts:23` estimate was wrong.** The first draft expected a new test there to kill 2 uncovered mutants. Both turned out to be equivalent once covered, so the after report shows one more survivor. The test is kept because it checks real behaviour (a missing host record must not break the attendee's restriction), not for the score.

- **Invalid source:** "The current output of your own code is not a valid source." A test whose expected value was copied from the code's output "cannot detect that the code is wrong."
- **"Not tested automatically, and why:"** is used only for ACs checked manually only.
- **"AI-written tests:"** should list "Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None.""

If you get errors, be sure to fix them before committing.

## Making a Pull Request

### Keep PRs Small and Focused

Large PRs are difficult to review and more prone to errors. We strongly encourage smaller, self-contained PRs:

- **Size limits**: Keep PRs under 500 lines of code changed and under 10 code files modified (excludes documentation, lock files, and auto-generated files)
- **Single responsibility**: Each PR should address one concern (one feature, one bug fix, or one refactor)
- **Split large changes**: If your task requires extensive changes, break it into multiple PRs that can be reviewed and merged independently

**How to split large changes:**
- Separate database/schema changes from application logic
- Split frontend and backend changes when possible
- Do preparatory refactoring in a separate PR before adding new features
- Create PRs in dependency order (infrastructure first, then features)

### PR Checklist

- Be sure to [check the "Allow edits from maintainers" option](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork) when creating your PR. (This option isn't available if you're [contributing from a fork belonging to an organization](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/5634))
- If your PR refers to or fixes an issue, add `refs #XXX` or `fixes #XXX` to the PR description. Replace `XXX` with the respective issue number. See more about [linking a pull request to an issue](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue).
- Fill out the PR template accordingly.
- Review the [App Contribution Guidelines](./packages/app-store/CONTRIBUTING.md) when building integrations.
- Lastly, make sure to keep your branches updated (e.g., click the `Update branch` button on the GitHub PR page).
== PR template

<!-- Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed. Please also include relevant motivation and context. List any dependencies that are required for this change.

Note: Cal.diy is a community-maintained open-source project. Contributions here do NOT flow to Cal.com's production service. -->

- Fixes #XXXX (GitHub issue number)

## Visual Demo (For contributors especially)

A visual demonstration is strongly recommended, for both the original and new change **(video / image - any one)**.

#### Video Demo (if applicable):

- Show screen recordings of the issue or feature.
- Demonstrate how to reproduce the issue, the behavior before and after the change.

#### Image Demo (if applicable):

- Add side-by-side screenshots of the original and updated change.
- Highlight any significant change(s).

## Mandatory Tasks (DO NOT REMOVE)

- [ ] I have self-reviewed the code (A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected).
- [ ] I have updated the developer docs if this PR makes changes that would require a documentation change. If N/A, write N/A here and check the checkbox.
- [ ] I confirm automated tests are in place that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.

<!-- Please describe the tests that you ran to verify your changes. Provide instructions so we can reproduce. Please also list any relevant details for your test configuration. Write details that help to start the tests -->

- What is expected (happy path) to have (input and output)?
- Any other important info that could help to test that PR

- I haven't commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- I haven't checked if my changes generate no new warnings
- My PR is too large (>500 lines or >10 files) and should be split into smaller PRs

```text
# Coding conventions
- Formatting/linting is enforced by Biome (`biome.json`): 110-char lines, 2-space indent, double quotes, semicolons always, es5 trailing commas, sorted imports. Run `yarn biome check --write .` before committing.
- TypeScript strict mode; use `import type { X }` for type-only imports; never use `as any`.
- Prisma queries use `select`, never `include` (performance + avoids leaking sensitive fields like `credential.key`).
- Import from source files directly, never through barrel `index.ts` files (e.g. `@calcom/ui/components/button`, not `@calcom/ui`).
- Errors: `ErrorWithCode` in services/repositories/utilities; `TRPCError` only inside tRPC routers.
- Early returns over nested conditionals.
- Comments explain **why**, never **what** - see [agents/rules/quality-code-comments.md](../../agents/rules/quality-code-comments.md).
- File naming: `Prisma<Entity>Repository.ts`, `<Entity>Service.ts` (PascalCase, no `.service.ts`/`.repository.ts` suffixes on new files).
- All user-facing strings go through `t()` and are added to `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.

- Before opening a PR, each contributor self-reviews their own diff for at least the items above - don't rely on CI/reviewers to catch a missed `as any` or a stray `include`.

# Branching and commit conventions

- Branch-based workflow, not forks - everyone has write access to the shared repo.
- `main` is protected; direct pushes are blocked. All changes go through a reviewed PR.
- Branch naming: `docs|feat|fix`/`name`
    + example: The branch that added this document is called `docs/standards-guidelines`
- Always branch from a freshly-pulled `main`.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`), referencing the issue number where relevant, e.g. `feat: add dark mode toggle (#17)`.
- Delete your branch after the PR merges.
- Never force-push or rebase shared/main branches.
- Commit names should be present tense description of largest changes.
    - `Add [insert big feature]`
    - `Remove [insert unneeded feature]`
    - `Fix [insert bug here]`

# Pull request process
Summarize your pull request at the top. Use the same prefix standard as branch names. (i.e. doc related PR would begin with `doc:`)

If your pull request addresses anything mentioned by existing issues, link those issues in your pull request description. For pull requests that are not ready to be reviewed, they must be prefixed with `WIP:` to indicate they are a work in progress, and therefore should not be reviewed for merging.
# Testing expectations
Testing the changes locally is the baseline expectation. Additionally, tests will need to be written for any new features added.

- New or modified code should carry **~80%+ test coverage**; aim for near-100% on isolated unit logic.
- Unit tests: Vitest, run with `TZ=UTC yarn test` (timezone-sensitive logic must be tested under UTC).
- E2E tests: Playwright — only required to run in CI when the PR carries the `ready-for-e2e` label.
- A PR is not "tested" until the automated tests proving the fix/feature actually pass locally.

# AI tool use
If a contributor utilizes artificial intelligence to generate code, they must **review every line generated** and have at least a basic working understanding of what the code does (i.e. an answer of "I don't know" to the question "what does this AI generated function do" would be unacceptable). The contributor also accepts full responsibility of any AI generated code. An AI agent **cannot be held accountable**.

![IBM training slides](https://cdn.lexza.ch/file/ffa6YaKwwn.png)

# Definition of Done

A change is "done" when:

- [ ] Code follows the conventions in [Section 1](#1-coding-conventions).
- [ ] `yarn type-check:ci --force` passes.
- [ ] `yarn biome check --write .` passes with no new warnings.
- [ ] Relevant unit tests pass (`TZ=UTC yarn test`); Playwright tests pass if applicable.
- [ ] Test coverage on new/changed code meets the ~80%+ expectation ([Section 4](#4-testing-expectations)).
- [ ] No secrets, API keys, or `.env` files are committed.
- [ ] No new UI strings without a corresponding translation key in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.
- [ ] PR follows the process in [Section 3](#3-pull-request-process): draft → self-reviewed → template filled out → issue linked (`Closes #<number>`) → within size limits.
- [ ] Any AI tool use is logged per [Section 5](#5-ai-tool-use).
- [ ] Documentation updated if the change affects developer-facing docs (or explicitly marked N/A).

# PR draft: feat(bookings): save and enforce minimum cancellation notice

Suggested title: `feat(bookings): save and enforce minimum cancellation notice for attendees (#150)`
Base: `main` · Head: `feat/issue-150-min-cancellation-notice-backend` · Open as **draft** · Milestone: **Sprint 3**

> **Before opening the PR, work through "Still to do before opening / merging" at the end of this draft.** The results
> below were verified on 2026-11-19 at commit `8222569`, whose code matches the current head (`dc774e0` added docs
> only). `main` has moved 10 commits since then (#144). That merge conflicts in one test file and hasn't been re-tested.

---

## What does this PR do?

- Closes #150
- Closes #139. #142 (merged) delivered the settings UI, and this PR completes the parent issue.

#142 added the "Minimum cancellation notice" setting behind the `minimum-cancellation-notice` flag. It kept the value
in component state, so nothing was saved or enforced. This PR makes the feature work end to end:

- **Saving:** a nullable `EventType.minimumCancellationNotice` column (minutes) and its migration. #142's setting now
  writes the event-type form, so the value saves and reloads, and switching it off saves `null`. Turning on **Disable
  Cancelling** also clears it, the same way Disable Rescheduling clears the reschedule notice.
- **Minutes or hours** (#139 AC1): a Minutes/Hours unit picker. The value is stored in minutes, and 1440 reopens as
  "24 hours".
- **Server enforcement:** `/api/cancel` rejects an attendee's cancellation inside the window with **403** and
  `code: "minimum_cancellation_notice"`. The check runs **before** the 5-minute soft-cancel task is queued.
- **Booking page:** inside the window, attendees see a translated "contact the host" message instead of Cancel. The
  `?cancel=true` email link shows the same message instead of the form.
- **Bookings list:** Cancel is disabled for attendees inside the window. This mirrors how the reschedule notice
  disables Reschedule there.
- **Hosts can always cancel.** "Host" means the organizer, or an event-type host who is on the booking. It's taken
  from the session only, never from the client-supplied `cancelledBy`.
- **Feature flag:** `minimum-cancellation-notice` switches the whole feature on or off.
- **Unchanged:** event types without a notice (every existing one), the reschedule notice, the 5-minute undo window,
  and API v2.
- **D6 mutation testing** for #139 is included: the configs, the before and after reports, and the write-up (see Test
  Evidence).

## Visual Demo

_To add: screenshots of the Advanced tab (setting with the Hours unit) and of the booking page message ("still to do"
item 5)._

## Design decisions

| Decision | Alternatives considered | Chosen, and why |
|---|---|---|
| Where to enforce | (a) `handleCancelBooking`; (b) both places, plus `requestedAt` in the task payload | **`/api/cancel` before `tasker.create`.** (a) runs 5 minutes later, after the attendee was told the cancel worked, and shifts the window by the delay. (b) needs more files and a payload change. |
| Who counts as host | (a) the organizer only; (b) the `cancelledBy` email | **The booking page's rule, using the session only.** (a) would block collective co-hosts. (b) can be faked from the URL. |
| Window after the start | Reuse `isWithinMinimumRescheduleNotice` | **A new helper that keeps blocking once the booking has started.** The reschedule helper stops at the start, but `handleCancelBooking` accepts cancellations until the end. |
| Minutes or hours | Minutes only (#142), or minutes/hours/days | **Minutes and Hours, stored as minutes.** #139 asks for "minutes or hours". Reuses the booking-notice pattern. |
| What the flag controls | Only hide the setting | **The whole feature.** Saved notices are ignored by `/api/cancel`, the booking page and the list while the flag is off, so no policy is enforced that the host can't see. |
| Translating the server error | Translate on the server, or English only | **A stable `code` that the cancel dialog maps to `t(...)`.** Anonymous requests have no locale, and API callers still get English. |
| Bookings list | Leave Cancel visible and rely on the server | **Disable Cancel**, the same way the reschedule notice disables Reschedule. |
| Recurring "cancel all remaining" | Cancel only the occurrences outside the window | **Reject if the earliest upcoming active occurrence is inside the window.** The alternative changes `handleCancelBooking`. |
| Where the logic lives | A full DI service (module, container, token) | **Pure functions, plus one function that takes an injected repository.** Testable without Prisma. |

These decisions answer #150's open questions. They were agreed in the implementation session on 2026-11-19. **They
still need to be posted on #150** ("still to do" item 2) so that "issue discussion" is a valid source of expected values.

## Test Evidence

The fork's CI fails at **Prepare** on every recent team PR (#140, #142, #144), before any tests run: _"Playwright does
not support chromium on ubuntu26.04-x64"_. So the commands and results are documented below, as the Sprint 3 rules
require when CI doesn't run the tests. **Completed** results and **pending** checks are listed separately.

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| **#150 AC1:** The setting is saved to the database and loaded when the event type settings are reopened. | `EventAdvancedTab.test.tsx` › shows the saved notice when the event type is reopened; saves the notice the host sets, in minutes (24 hours → `1440`) · `MinimumCancellationNoticeController.test.tsx` › loads the saved notice from the event type form; writes the notice into the event type form as a change to save · `useEventTypeForm.test.ts` › loads a stored value of 1440 / null / undefined; saves a newly set notice · `eventTypes/__tests__/types.test.ts` › accepts 1440 / 1 / 0 / null; rejects -1 / 1.5 / "60"; leaves the stored notice untouched when omitted · **Manual (B):** as host `teampro`, saved 1440 through the real tRPC update → the DB column is 1440 and `eventTypes.get` returns 1440 | unit, manual | AC; other (24 h × 60 = 1440 minutes; the column stores whole minutes ≥ 0) |
| **#150 AC2:** Turning off the setting clears the notice. | `EventAdvancedTab.test.tsx` › saves no notice when the host switches the setting off; clears the saved notice when Disable Cancelling is turned on · `MinimumCancellationNoticeController.test.tsx` › clears the saved notice when switched off; clears the saved notice when 'Always allow' is chosen; does not change the form when only switched on · `useEventTypeForm.test.ts` › clears the notice when the setting is turned off · **Manual (E):** saved `null` through tRPC → the column is NULL and reloads as `null` | unit, manual | AC; upstream behavior (Disable Rescheduling clears the reschedule notice in `DisableReschedulingController`) |

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- **The host rule now exists in three places:** `isUserBookingHost` (new), `checkIfUserIsHost` in the booking page's
  server props, and `checkIfUserIsHost` in the bookings-list handler. I kept them separate to limit the diff and avoid
  refactoring code this issue doesn't need. The risk is that they drift apart.
- **Redundant defensive checks.** Examples: `?.` on fields that are always set (`session.user`, `loggedInUser`), and a
  second `<= 0` guard in `getMinimumCancellationNoticeViolation`. D6 found that they produce 12 equivalent mutants, and
  they could be simplified.
- **The server error message is English only** for API callers. The UI translates it through the `code` field.
- **`/api/cancel` builds its repositories directly** (`new BookingRepository(prisma)`, `new FeaturesRepository(prisma)`)
  instead of using a DI container. This follows the other `apps/web/app/api` routes. The booking page's server props
  and `/api/cancel` each now make one flag lookup per request (cached for 5 minutes).
- **`isMinimumCancellationNoticeEnabled` is optional** in `BookingActionContext`, so other code that builds the context
  didn't need to change. A missing value means off.
- **One undecided behaviour:** turning Disable Cancelling **off** keeps a saved notice. That combination can only be
  saved through the API, and no requirement covers it (a D6 test gap, documented).
- **The bookings list disables Cancel without explaining why.** On the recurring tab it judges by the row's start time;
  the server still checks the earliest occurrence.
- **D6 tooling:** `stryker.139.config.mjs` and `vitest.stryker-139.config.mts` are committed alongside the shared config.

**Encountered:**

- **CI is broken for every team PR.** The Prepare job fails ("Playwright does not support chromium on
  ubuntu26.04-x64"). I documented local commands and results instead.
- **`yarn type-check:ci --force` fails on Windows** (`spawn tsc ENOENT`). I used `npx tsc` per package.
  `packages/features` has 89 pre-existing type errors. I left them alone, because none are in this PR's files.
- **The feature-flag cache never clears.** `FeaturesRepository` caches all flags per process for 5 minutes, and the
  admin toggle doesn't clear it, so any flag change takes up to 5 minutes to reach server checks. Found in manual
  check D and documented, not fixed.
- **`PermissionCheckService` is a stub in this fork,** so team admins never see other members' bookings. That made an
  "admin exemption" question moot.
- **Pre-existing skipped tests:** 2 in `confirm.handler.test.ts`. Not touched.
- **Local tooling:** Biome expects LF but `core.autocrlf=true` creates CRLF working copies, so every changed file shows a
  false `format` error locally. I compared against `main` with line endings normalized. The pre-commit hook regenerates
  app-store `*.generated.*` files and could stage unrelated formatting changes, so I checked each commit's file list.
- **Parallel edits on `main`:** merge conflicts with #140 (`BookingRepository.ts`, resolved) and #144
  (`bookingActions.test.ts`, still to resolve).

**Remaining limitations and coverage gaps:**

- The booking page has no rendering test (37 no-coverage mutants). The data-selection lines need a database (7
  no-coverage). There are 7 documented D6 test gaps (styling, the unit picker's `isSearchable`, and the Disable
  Cancelling case above).
- An attendee can reschedule to a later slot and then cancel. Hosts can close this with the existing reschedule
  notice.
- API v2 cancellations are not restricted (out of scope).
- Near the boundary, the browser's clock and the server's clock may disagree. The server decides, and the user sees the
  translated error.
- The confirmation email doesn't mention the policy (#150 open question, out of scope).
- The D6 line numbers refer to commit `8222569`. Merging the current `main` shifts some of them; the reports stay valid
  for that commit.

**Recommended future improvements:**

1. Move the booking page's cancellation decision into a tested helper or hook, or build a render-test harness for the
   page. This would cover the 37 no-coverage mutants.
2. Merge the three host-rule copies into one shared helper.
3. Remove the redundant guards (D6's equivalent mutants), with the tests unchanged.
4. Decide, record and test what turning Disable Cancelling off does to a saved notice.
5. Clear `FeaturesRepository`'s cache when a flag is toggled.
6. Fix the CI runner image or Playwright version so team PRs get automated checks again.
7. Add database integration tests for the new repository queries.
8. Follow-up issues: API v2 support, an explanation for the disabled Cancel in `/bookings`, and the policy in
   confirmation emails.

**This PR does not meet the team limit.** Even counting production code only, it touches **21 files**, against a limit

Justification for keeping it as one PR:
- 11 of the 21 production files are 1–2-line wiring that the type system requires (selects, types, defaults).
- About 70% of the lines are tests.
- D6 measured one combined mutation scope, so its reports and write-up belong with this code.

**PR(s):** [#144](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/144)  **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 with the Vitest runner  **Config:** [stryker.137.config.mjs](../../../stryker.137.config.mjs) + [vitest.stryker-137.config.mts](../../../vitest.stryker-137.config.mts), built on the shared [stryker.config.mjs](../../../stryker.config.mjs) by @zach-short and following the per-issue layout of `stryker.138.config.mjs` by @lexzach  **Command:** `STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/137-kojoshuay-<before|after>.json TZ=UTC nvm exec 22 node_modules/.bin/stryker run stryker.137.config.mjs`

**Note:** line numbers below refer to commit `974a231`. After review, `sendNotice` returns `recipientCount` instead of `sent`, so a few lines moved.


## Surviving mutants

All 11 survivors from the before report are in lines this PR added.

| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RunningLateService.ts:64` | `if (recipients.length === 0) return { sent: 0 }` → `if (false)` | Equivalent | Without the early return, `Promise.allSettled([])` resolves to `[]`, no email is built, nothing is logged, and the method still returns `{ sent: 0 }`. The behavior is the same; the early return only skips work. |
| `RunningLateService.ts:72` | `getTranslation(locale, "common")` → `getTranslation(locale, "")` | Test gap (killed after) | The `running_late_*` email strings are in the `common` namespace. With any other namespace the attendee's email would show raw keys. The test's `getTranslation` mock ignored its second argument, so nothing checked the namespace. |
| `RunningLateService.ts:87` | `if (failures.length > 0)` → `if (true)` | Test gap (killed after) | Would log an error after every successful send. No test checked that a clean send logs nothing. |
| `RunningLateService.ts:87` | `if (failures.length > 0)` → `if (false)` | Test gap (killed after) | Emails that fail before sending (loading translations or building the email) would go unlogged. The method swallows these failures so the host's request still succeeds, so this log is the only record of them. SMTP failures never reach it: `BaseEmail.sendEmail` logs and swallows those itself. No test checked it. |
| `RunningLateService.ts:87` | `failures.length > 0` → `failures.length <= 0` | Test gap (killed after) | Logs only when nothing failed: the opposite of the intent. Same missing assertions as the two rows above. |
| `RunningLateService.ts:87` | `failures.length > 0` → `failures.length >= 0` | Test gap (killed after) | Always logs, like `if (true)`. |
| `RunningLateService.ts:87` | `if` body → `{}` | Test gap (killed after) | Removes the log entirely, like `if (false)`. |
| `RunningLateService.ts:88` | log message → `` ` ` `` (empty) | Test gap (killed after) | The message is how on-call staff find which booking's emails failed. No test checked its content. |
| `RunningLateService.ts:88` | `{ reasons: [...] }` → `{}` | Test gap (killed after) | Drops the failure reasons (for example "SMTP down") from the log. Not asserted. |
| `RunningLateService.ts:89` | `(failure) => String(failure.reason)` → `() => undefined` | Test gap (killed after) | Logs `[undefined]` instead of the reasons. Not asserted. |
| `bookingActions.ts:192` | `booking.loggedInUser?.userId` → `booking.loggedInUser.userId` | Equivalent | `loggedInUser` is a required (non-optional) field of `BookingItemProps` (`apps/web/components/booking/types.ts:12`), so it is never `undefined` and `?.` behaves exactly like `.`. A test with no `loggedInUser` would have to break the type to build that input. |

## New or strengthened test

Commit: [PR #144](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/144/files) · Test: `packages/features/bookings/services/RunningLateService.test.ts` › keeps sending to other attendees when one email fails · Kills: `RunningLateService.ts:87` (`if (false)`)

## Questions

**1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**

The suriving mutants revealed that my tests checked what the code returned, but there was a gap in testing dependencies. There were two main blind spots in RunningLateService.test.ts:

1) sendNotice is the backend service method in RunningLateService that is run when the host clicks the Running Late button on a booking. It sends an email to each attendee of the event, logs errors from building an email (SMTP errors are logged by the shared email class instead), and at the time returned the number of emails it counted as sent. In my original code, the tests checked that sendNotice returned that count, but the tests did not check the server log errors. This means that if someone tried to break or delete the log later there would be no warning from the tests. 

2) The convention in this Cal codebase to translate text is to use the getTranslation function. This function nees two arguements: local (the attendee's langauge) and "common" (the namespace of what translation file to load). To test this, a mock helper was created so the test does not nee to load the real translation file from the disk. However, the fake function only accpeted the locale parameter and did not accept the namespace parameter. The gap is that the test was too forigving. The test passes on whatever namespace is, even if it is broken. 

**2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.**

The gap #2 mentioned in the previos question answers this question. The original test had the assertion: 

expect(ana.t("running_late")).toBe("ja:running_late");

However, the requirements does not say that emails should output "ja:running_late". The actual requreiemnt is that each attendee gets the email in their own language using Cal.com's real translations, what are in the "common" namsespace. 

**3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct?**

I used Claude Code.

- **Configuration:** it cherry-picked @zach-short's shared Stryker setup onto my branch and wrote `stryker.137.config.mjs` and `vitest.stryker-137.config.mts` from @lexzach's issue-138 versions. It read the commit diff to find the exact line range my PR added to `bookingActions.ts`.
- **Running:** the machine's default Node is 20, and Stryker 10 needs Node 22, so it installed Node 22 with nvm and ran Stryker through `nvm exec 22`.
- **Analysis:** it classified the 11 survivors.
- **Tests:** it wrote the strengthened tests.
1) keeps sending to other attendess when on emails fails:
  - Strengthed the test to also check for service logs the booking ID and exact fail reason. This is to record in the server of emails that were not sent

2) does not log an error when every email sends:

- this is a new test verify that there is no error log message for when all emails were sent succesfully.

3) uses each attendee's own locale and time zone

- Before, this test ignored which translation file the service asked for. Strengthend to now asking for the "common" translation fie so the email has real words, not raw keys. 

- **Verified:**
  - The three selected test files passed before mutation (87 tests), and again after the change (88 tests).
  - Both reports contain the same 108 mutants at the same locations.
  - All 9 "test gap" survivors show as Killed in the after report.
  - The scores in this file match Stryker's summary table (91/102 = 89.22%, 100/102 = 98.04%).
- **Checked the equivalence claims:**
  - `loggedInUser` really is a required field in `types.ts`.
  - With an empty recipient list, the code after the early return produces `{ sent: 0 }` with no side effects.

For human verification of myself, I read over the report to understand the gaps by myself. I also manually ran the test files on my laptop to make sure all tests passed. Same workflow as Sprint 2 (D4), including the Tech Debt section. Sprint 3 adds a Test Evidence section to every PR description. It replaces the "how it was tested" part of the description, so you don't write it twice.


## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: ... | ... | ... | ... |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** [...]

**AI-written tests:** [Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you
checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None."]
How to fill it in:

One row per acceptance criterion from D2. For bug reports, use the Expected Behavior instead. For PRs that change no product behavior (for example, CI changes), write "N/A" and explain why.
Test(s): the test name (and file, if not obvious). If you checked the AC manually, write Manual: followed by the steps and what you saw. If an AC is tested both automatically and manually, list both in the same row.
Level: unit, integration, E2E, or manual.
Source of expected value: where the expected result in your test comes from. Use one of: AC, issue discussion, docs, upstream behavior, or other (explain). The current output of your own code is not a valid source; a test whose expected value was copied from what the code returns cannot detect that the code is wrong.
Not tested automatically, and why: only for ACs checked manually only.
You may use AI to draft this section, but you are responsible for checking that it is accurate.

## What does this PR do?

- Closes #150
- Closes #139. #142 (merged) added the settings UI, and this PR completes the parent issue.

#142 added the **Minimum cancellation notice** setting behind the `minimum-cancellation-notice` flag. It kept the value
in component state, so nothing was saved or enforced. This PR makes the feature work end to end: attendees can no
longer cancel within the host's notice window, and hosts can always cancel.

- **Saving:** a new nullable `EventType.minimumCancellationNotice` column (minutes) and its migration. #142's setting
  now writes to the event-type form, so the value saves, reloads when the event type is reopened, and becomes `null`
  when switched off. Turning on **Disable Cancelling** also clears it, the same way Disable Rescheduling clears the
  reschedule notice.
- **Minutes or hours:** a Minutes/Hours unit picker (#139 AC1). The value is stored in minutes, and 1440 reopens as
  "24 hours".
- **Server enforcement:** `/api/cancel` rejects an attendee's cancellation inside the window with **403** and
  `code: "minimum_cancellation_notice"`. The check runs **before** the 5-minute soft-cancel task is queued.
- **Booking page:** inside the window, attendees see a translated "contact the host" message instead of Cancel. The
  `?cancel=true` email link shows the same message instead of the cancel form.
- **Bookings list (`/bookings`):** Cancel is disabled for attendees inside the window.
- **Hosts:** the organizer, or an event-type host who is on the booking. Identified from the session only, never from
  the client-supplied `cancelledBy`.
- **Feature flag:** `minimum-cancellation-notice` turns the whole feature on and off. While it's off, saved notices are
  ignored.
- **Unchanged:** event types without a notice (every existing one), the reschedule notice, the 5-minute undo window,
  and API v2.
- **D6 mutation testing for #139:** `stryker.139.config.mjs`, `vitest.stryker-139.config.mts`, the before and after
  reports, and the write-up in `docs/sprint3/mutation/139-julissaehp.md`.

## Design

| Decision | Options considered | Chosen, and why |
|---|---|---|
| **Where to enforce** | (a) inside `handleCancelBooking`; (b) in `/api/cancel` before the task is queued; (c) both places, plus `requestedAt` in the task | **(b).** `handleCancelBooking` runs 5 minutes after the request. The attendee would already have been told the cancellation worked, and the window would shift by the delay. (c) needs more files and changes the task payload. |
| **Who counts as a host** | (a) the organizer only; (b) the `cancelledBy` email; (c) the booking page's rule (organizer, or an event-type host on the booking), using the session | **(c).** (a) would block collective co-hosts that the page shows Cancel to. (b) can be faked from the URL. |
| **After the booking starts** | (a) reuse `isWithinMinimumRescheduleNotice`, which stops blocking at the start; (b) a new helper that keeps blocking until the end | **(b).** `handleCancelBooking` accepts cancellations until the booking ends, so (a) would let attendees cancel a meeting in progress. |
| **Units** | (a) minutes only, as in #142; (b) minutes or hours, stored as minutes; (c) minutes, hours or days | **(b).** #139 AC1 asks for "minutes or hours". (b) reuses the booking notice's unit pattern. |
| **What the feature flag controls** | (a) only hide the setting; (b) the whole feature | **(b).** With (a), turning the flag off would leave a policy enforced that the host can no longer see or clear. |
| **Translating the server error** | (a) translate on the server; (b) English only; (c) a stable `code` that the cancel dialog translates | **(c).** Anonymous requests have no locale, and API callers still get a readable English message. |
| **Bookings list** | (a) leave Cancel visible and rely on the server error; (b) disable Cancel inside the window | **(b).** It matches how the reschedule notice disables Reschedule in the same list. |
| **"Cancel all remaining"** | (a) cancel only the occurrences outside the window; (b) reject if the earliest upcoming occurrence is inside the window | **(b).** (a) would change `handleCancelBooking`'s semantics. |

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- **The host rule exists in three places:** the new `isUserBookingHost`, `checkIfUserIsHost` in the booking page's
  server props, and `checkIfUserIsHost` in the bookings-list handler. I kept them separate to limit the diff; they
  could drift apart.
- **Redundant defensive checks.** Examples: `?.` on fields that are always set, and a second `<= 0` guard. D6 showed
  these produce equivalent mutants, so they can be simplified.
- **The server's error message is English only** for API callers. The UI translates it through `code`.
- **`/api/cancel` builds `BookingRepository` and `FeaturesRepository` directly**, as other `app/api` routes do, instead
  of using DI. The booking page and `/api/cancel` each now do one flag lookup per request (cached for 5 minutes).
- **`isMinimumCancellationNoticeEnabled` is optional** in `BookingActionContext`, so other code that builds the context
  didn't need to change. A missing value means off.
- **One undecided behavior.** Turning Disable Cancelling **off** keeps a saved notice. That state can only be created
  through the API, and no requirement covers it.
- **The bookings list disables Cancel without explaining why.** On the recurring tab it judges by the row's start
  time; the server still checks the earliest occurrence.

**Encountered:**
- **CI fails at Prepare on every team PR** (Playwright doesn't support the runner's Ubuntu image). I documented the
  local commands and results instead.
- **`yarn type-check:ci --force` doesn't run on Windows.** I ran `npx tsc` per package instead. `packages/features`
  has 89 pre-existing type errors; none are in this PR's files, so I left them.
- **`FeaturesRepository` caches all flags for 5 minutes, and the admin toggle doesn't clear the cache**, so flag
  changes take up to 5 minutes to reach server checks. Documented, not fixed.
- **`PermissionCheckService` is a stub in this fork**, so team admins never see other members' bookings.
- **Two pre-existing skipped tests** in `confirm.handler.test.ts`. Not touched.
- **Merge conflicts from parallel edits** with #140 (`BookingRepository.ts`) and #144 (`bookingActions.test.ts`).
  Resolved by keeping both sides, then re-tested.

**Remaining limitations:**
- The booking page has no rendering test (37 no-coverage mutants in D6).
- An attendee can reschedule to a later slot and then cancel. Hosts can close this with the reschedule notice.
- API v2 cancellations aren't restricted (out of scope).
- The confirmation email doesn't mention the policy.

## Checklist

- My PR is too large (>500 lines or >10 files) and should be split into smaller PRs.

  **Size:** 38 files and 1,948 changed lines:

  | Category | Files | Lines |
  |---|---|---|
  | Production code | 21 | 352 |
  | Tests | 9 + 1 helper | 1,221 |
  | Stryker config | 2 | 78 |
  | Docs and reports | 4 | 293 |
  | `common.json` | 1 | 4 |

  This exceeds the team's 10-file limit. I kept it as one PR because:
  - 11 of the production files are 1–2 line wiring that the type system requires;
  - 74% of the code lines are tests;
  - the D6 reports cover this combined change.

  If a split is wanted, it divides cleanly: (1) persistence and the settings wiring, (2) enforcement and the booking
  page, (3) the bookings list.

     export function isWithinMinimumCancellationNotice({ startTime, minimumCancellationNotice, now = new Date() }) {
       if (!minimumCancellationNotice || minimumCancellationNotice <= 0 || !startTime) return false;
       const msUntilStart = new Date(startTime).getTime() - now.getTime();
       return msUntilStart < minimumCancellationNotice * MS_PER_MINUTE;
     }
     export function isUserBookingHost({ userId, bookingUserId, attendeeEmails, eventTypeHosts }) { if (!userId) return false; if (bookingUserId === userId) return true; ... }

     export async function getMinimumCancellationNoticeViolation({ bookingRepository, bookingUid, userId, allRemainingBookings, now })
     ```
